## p122 A2 — Continuation asking about Constanza cable and AOK 11 communications

**Edition context:** November 4: repeated-part request and communications inquiry.

**Related source pages:** [p121 A1](121.md#source-p121-a1), [p121 A2](121.md#source-p121-a2), [p121 B1](121.md#source-p121-b1).

<a id="edition-cases-radio-nov4-repetition-and-connections-november-4-repeated-part-request-and-communications-inquiry"></a>



**Source edition and verification: icekylinx and GPT-6 Astra Pro.**

The four records preserve two messages with different source frames. All use the unchanged published Nov4–6 key. No group is added, dropped, moved or reordered; all numerical and reference labels remain literal.

The two p121 A parts have the header `FUER COS 1955 (4.11) 2 TL`, explicitly address `GENERAL VON KRESS KAUKASUS`, and are recorded at `03.13 a.m., November 5th` under the November 4 page heading. The discrepancy is retained.

<a id="edition-cases-radio-nov4-repetition-and-connections-interpretation-attribution-and-evidence"></a>

### Interpretation, attribution and evidence

The first message asks for the **first part** again; it does not identify that missing part in this collection or establish that the request was fulfilled. `Z A 1 K C`, `G A 1 RM 2 ANG`, `8538.18`, `AKONACH 18`, `111511` and `95086` are retained without a new numeral or office interpretation. `U` and `NACHRICHEF` remain the encoded abbreviations.

Earlier unreviewed repository candidates already identified these bodies. This edition corrects OCR against the scan, preserves the actual printed glyphs and prices every proposed coordinate change; it makes no first-decipherment claim. The published key keeps its original provenance.

#### Two parts on different pages

p121 B1 and p122 A2 both print `FUER UKS (4.11) 0035 2 TLE` with parts `1 TL` and `2 TL`. Their recorded reception times are `06.55 a.m.` and `05.25 p.m., November 4th`. These matching source labels and the grammatical continuation support the pairing. The page-local letters B and A remain in their physical record identifiers.

## p122 B — Trade Minister asks whether von Schorlemer can join demobilization work

**Edition context:** Von Schorlemer: demobilization work inquiry and reply.

**Related source pages:** [p155 B](155.md#source-p155-b).

<a id="edition-cases-people-schorlemer-demobilization-inquiry-von-schorlemer-demobilization-work-inquiry-and-reply"></a>



**Source review and edition: icekylinx and GPT-6 Astra Pro.**

A clear-address request on p122 and an encrypted reply on p155 form a source-linked exchange about von Schorlemer's availability for demobilization work. The earlier request asks whether he can be released to the Trade Ministry; the later administrative-staff reply says he cannot currently be spared. Both native frames and every repair remain explicit. The later reply supports the name and topic; the 33 supplied mask values in the first request remain editorial proposals.

<a id="source-p122-b"></a>
<a id="edition-cases-people-schorlemer-demobilization-inquiry-p122-b"></a>

### p122 B

**Source transcription — header:** `B) NKJ v LP (08.40 p.m., November 4th); FUER UKS 1400 (4). OBERLEUTNANT VON SCHORLEMER OBERKOMMANDO M VERWALTUNGSSTAB; RICHI-252`

**Readable German** — based on the explicitly repaired output below.

> Erbitte Rueckantwort durch Funkspruch, ob Sie zur Beschaeftigung im Handelsministerium, Demobilmachungsgruppe, abkoemmlich. Handelsminister.

**Meaning:** The Trade Minister asks for a radio reply on whether the addressee can be released for work in the ministry demobilization group. The clear header names First Lieutenant von Schorlemer at the Oberkommando M administrative staff.

### Evidence and credit

Published period keys: George Lasry, Ingo Niebel, Nils Kopal and Arno Wacker (2016), and George Lasry (2017 key list). Earlier unreviewed repository candidates are retained separately. Source review and explicit editorial work: icekylinx and GPT-6 Astra Pro.

The certificates replay every coordinate alteration, compare the independent column/domain reconstruction with the cipher implementation, and re-encrypt every complete edited output. For a partial output, an injective global completion of the square and residual source masks supplies an explicitly nonhistorical roundtrip witness. Each readable passage preserves every nonseparator output label; literal protected fields are also checked without removing their internal separators. Source crops are bound to the original PDF by page, rectangle, scale, file digest and RGB-pixel digest.

Reproduce with `python experiments/schorlemer_demobilization_inquiry/verify.py --verify`. Add `--pdf /path/to/adfgvx-childs.pdf` to regenerate and compare the delivered source pixels.

A roundtrip proves compatibility with a stated reading. Editorial spelling repairs remain proposals, and literal number labels are not automatically historical dates, quantities or reference numbers.

### Source limits and attribution

The header reads `NKJ v LP (08.42 p.m., November 4th)` and `FUER UKS 1405 (4).`; the ciphertext label is `RICHI-114`. The 114 source coordinates give **57/57 fixed positions**, with no repair, fill or change of key. The address and signature abbreviations are not expanded into an asserted historical identity. This acknowledgment is not used to decide the route or amount of any other money message.

An earlier unreviewed repository OCR candidate already supplies the body. This is the source-audited edition, with original key credit preserved and no first-solution assertion. ## p122 D suffix — Repeat of the Feigenhaus instruction, part 1

**Edition context:** p120 / p123 - Three-part instruction to Feigenhaus.

**Related source pages:** [p120 B1](120.md#source-p120-b1), [p123 A2](123.md#source-p123-a2), [p123 A3](123.md#source-p123-a3).

<a id="edition-cases-naval-p120-p123-p120--p123---three-part-instruction-to-feigenhaus"></a>


[Source records](../../experiments/corpus_readings/selected_sources.json)

**Records:** p120 B1, the repeated suffix p122 D, and p123 A2-A3.
**Result:** an assembled three-part message under the published Nov4-6 key.
The 461-position reading below is conditional on the repairs in the table:
five valid-coordinate substitutions, nineteen erasure fills and one deletion.
The names and unusual expressions remain literal; their intended referents
have not been established.

**Prior body reading:** George Lasry, Ingo Niebel, Nils Kopal and Arno Wacker
already describe the three-part Feigenhaus/Herkules message in §6.5 of
[*Deciphering ADFGVX messages from the Eastern Front of World War I*](https://doi.org/10.1080/01611194.2016.1169461),
printed p24 / author-PDF p25. The present contribution by **icekylinx and
GPT-6 Astra Pro** is the source-level edition, exact repair accounting and
identification of the p122 D repeated suffix. This includes the inherited
prior body of that suffix; it is not a first decipherment of the message.

<a id="edition-cases-naval-p120-p123-most-likely-reading"></a>

### Most likely reading

**Readable German:**

> Feigenhaus, Konstantinopel. Sechshundertsiebzehn. Beichtvater
> zweihundertdreiundneunzig. Nachdem Diktator Anweisung gegeben,
> Notschreie in Andreas nicht vorzunehmen, haben wir uns nochmals mit
> Herkules in Verbindung gesetzt.
>
> Herkules ablehnt Verantwortung fuer neue Notschreie. Infolgedessen
> koennen wir auf keinen Fall neue Notschreie in Andreas vornehmen.
>
> Sie wollen deshalb unseren Anweisungen entsprechend sich verhalten.
> Drahtet, was ihr in Anbetracht veraenderter politischer Lage nunmehr
> zu tun gedenkt. Reichsversorgung.

**Meaning:** The sender reports renewed contact with Herkules after Diktator
instructed that no further *Notschreie* be undertaken in Andreas. Herkules
declines responsibility, so the prohibition stands. The recipient is to follow
these instructions and telegraph the action now intended in view of the
changed political situation. The opening names Feigenhaus in Constantinople
and the references 617 and 293, written out as words in the ciphertext.

*Notschreie* literally means cries for help. Together with Feigenhaus,
Beichtvater, Diktator, Andreas, Herkules and Reichsversorgung, it may belong
to a special vocabulary. This edition does not substitute guessed people,
places, institutions or operations for these terms. The irregular telegram
word order and the shift from *Sie* to *ihr* are retained. Word spacing,
punctuation and capitalization are editorial.

<a id="edition-cases-naval-p120-p123-source-support"></a>

It is not decrypted as a separate short message: changing the transposition
frame to 164 would change the column boundaries.

`VAAXX VXXAVA`. Deleting source index **211 or 212** gives the same repaired
stream. Among all 297 one-coordinate deletions, these are the only two
minimizers for the **stated candidate**, each requiring two further
valid-coordinate substitutions. This candidate-specific check does not
prove that every possible German reading has been considered.

<a id="edition-cases-naval-p120-p123-assembly-dates-and-credit"></a>

### Assembly, dates and credit

The source labels the parts `1 TL`, `2 TL`, `3 TL` and `3 TEILE`.
The p120 header is `OSM v OUI (8.32 p.m., November 4th); 1956`;
p122 repeats its suffix at 8.33 p.m. with `1056`, and p123 supplies parts 2
and 3 at 8.40 p.m., also with `1056`. The differing four-digit fields are
retained. The route, part labels and exact repeated suffix support the
assembly. No date is changed to fit the period key.

The source is J. Rives Childs, *General Solution of the ADFGVX Cipher
System*, printed pp. 120, 122-123 / PDF pp. 123, 125-126 in the
[public scan](https://drive.google.com/file/d/1_JiNMck7eUvdrOTrH7fsj1Yh44t-VSC6/view).
The complete Nov4-6 key retains its attribution to George Lasry and the
historical/research sources in [the key register](../../data/keys.json).
Source assembly, inspection, repair accounting and this edition:
**icekylinx and GPT-6 Astra Pro**. No first historical decipherment priority
is claimed.
